title: A 56-to-64GHz Linear Power Amplifier with 30.2dBm Psat and 23.5% PAEpeak Using Scalable Matched-Zone-Expanding Radial Power Combining with EM-Loss Reduction in 40nm Bulk CMOS
problem: High mm-wave frequencies (V-band, 56–64GHz) for 5G NR FR2-2 and SATCOM require high-power, high-efficiency power amplifiers in voltage-limited silicon processes. Traditional voltage-mode and current-mode power combining face impedance mismatches as combining scales (Zopt changes with combining ratio), limiting PA core selection. Passive combiner losses increase significantly with scale due to routing parasitics, and transistor efficiency degrades at high mm-wave due to parasitic capacitance and fT/fmax limitations.
motivation: 5G millimeter-wave and satellite communications demand high linear output power (>30dBm) with high efficiency (>20% PAE) to support multi-Gb/s modulation schemes; silicon integration is essential for cost and integration.
method: The power amplifier uses a radial power combiner to merge outputs from multiple transistor cores, arranging them in a circular geometry that reduces parasitic losses compared to linear routing. It employs matched-zone expansion—a technique that maintains constant electrical impedance across combining stages, preventing the efficiency losses that normally occur when scaling to more cores. Electromagnetic optimization and parasitic minimization further reduce losses. The design delivers 30.2dBm output power at 23.5% peak power-added efficiency, measuring how much input power converts to useful output versus waste heat.
key_novelty: A radial power combiner with matched-zone expansion—maintaining constant electrical impedance as you scale up the design—enables high-power, high-efficiency amplifiers at millimeter-wave V-band frequencies without the efficiency loss that has constrained prior designs.
contributions: Output power: 30.2dBm Psat at 56–64GHz (high linear power)
Peak PAE: 23.5% (high efficiency for V-band power amplifier)
Scalable matched-zone-expanding radial combiner maintaining impedance optimization across scales
EM-loss reduction via parasitic-aware layout achieving efficiency gain over traditional combining
primary_theme: High-efficiency V-band power amplifier via scalable radial power combining
